chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Remembering the song 'Tight Like That'
summary: Johnston and Gil try to recall the 1920s song and the mother who forbade her to sing it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I remember, I had absolutely no idea what the lyrics meant at the time, but I was a little girl, a little girl in elementary school when the song, 'Type Like That' right came out. And I remember one Sunday when......
How's that go?
Oh I couldn't sing it any more to save my life. And I'll tell you what........
Must be a second one. Tight Like That'?
Yes, I saw the lyrics to it the other day and I happen to have them here somewhere.
I remember there was an old Tight Like That', but that was......
Oh this is back in the twenties.
Oh yes?
Oh yes, back in the twenties.
It was the blues, right?
Well it was a jazzy kind of thing as I remember it. But I...
I remember one that went something like this. (PLAYS PIANO). Was it blues like that? (PLAYS PIANO).
Yes, yes, it was a thing like that. Yes, it was.
Like that, yes. There was more beat to it. (PLAYS PIANO). Something like that? (PLAYS PIANO).
Yes, yes.
I remember, who sang that now?
Mm
One of the reasons that I don't remember the song is that my very, very distinguished mother was sitting on our front porch with guests and I came out singing 'Type Like That'. (LAUGHTER).
And my mother told me, never to ever sing that song again. And of course I.....

MRS. JOHNSTON: It was rather a beauty and I simply did not. But I think that this has brought out a very important point here and that is that there is a sexual association and there is a............ .......(VOICE FADES OUT).
